title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.7: Beating LLL

problems.sourceStatement: Consider a matrix where both columns are rows are t-sparse. LLL gives a discrepancy bound of $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ here. If we assume the stronger property that every pair of rows intersect in at most one element, can we get a $O(\sqrt{t})$?
problems.problem: For 0-1 matrices (set systems) in which every row and every column has at most $t$ non-zero entries (both rows and columns $t$-sparse), determine whether the additional hypothesis that any two rows intersect in at most one element (a simple / linear hypergraph) yields a discrepancy bound of $O(\sqrt{t})$, or at least $o(\sqrt{t\log t})$, improving on the Lovász Local Lemma bound $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$.
problems.wordDescription: For a $t$-sparse 0-1 matrix (each element lies in at most $t$ sets and each set has size at most $t$), a folklore application of the Lovász Local Lemma gives discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$: a random coloring is analyzed per row and the dependencies are controlled by the sparsity. The question asks whether the 'simple hypergraph' condition — any two sets intersect in at most one element — removes the $\sqrt{\log t}$ factor, giving the Beck-Fiala-conjecture bound $O(\sqrt{t})$ in this special case. This is a special case of the Beck-Fiala conjecture, and the Beck-Fiala conjecture is open even for this very special case of simple hypergraphs (any two sets intersect in at most one element). No progress or resolution of this specific question was found in the literature as of 2026.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Let $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ be the incidence matrix of a set system $\mathcal{S} = \{S_1, \dots, S_m\}$ on $[n]$ that is $t$-sparse in both directions: every element lies in at most $t$ sets and every set has at most $t$ elements. Call $\mathcal{S}$ simple (linear) if $|S_j \cap S_k| \leq 1$ for all $j \neq k$. Write $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = \min_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n}\|Ax\|_\infty$, and let $L(t) = \sup \mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S})$ over all doubly $t$-sparse simple systems (any $n, m$) and $D(t) = \sup \mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S})$ over all doubly $t$-sparse systems. Benchmarks. For doubly $t$-sparse systems each set intersects at most $t(t-1)$ others, so the Lovász Local Lemma (LLL) applied to a uniformly random coloring gives $D(t) = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ (the bound recorded on the AimPL page), independent of $n$ and $m$; the Beck-Fiala theorem gives $D(t) \leq 2t - 1$ and $\Omega(\sqrt{t}) \leq L(t) \leq D(t)$ (lower bound e.g. from the incidence system of a projective plane of order $t - 1$, which is simple, $t$-regular and has discrepancy $\Omega(\sqrt{t})$ by the eigenvalue bound). Bounds depending on $n$: Bansal-Jiang 2025 and Altschuler-Tikhomirov 2026 give $O(\sqrt{t})$ for $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$ and $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for all $t$ (Problem 1.15), which beats the LLL bound only for $t$ at least polylogarithmic in $n$; for random $t$-sparse systems $O(\sqrt{t})$ holds w.h.p. (Potukuchi 2018; Bansal-Meka 2019; Problem 1.2). No bound $o(\sqrt{t \log t})$ depending only on $t$ is known for simple doubly $t$-sparse systems. Question (as posed). Is $L(t) = O(\sqrt{t})$? More generally, can the LLL bound $O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ be improved for doubly $t$-sparse systems under the simplicity hypothesis, and can such colorings be found efficiently? Complete resolution. A proof that $L(t) \leq C\sqrt{t}$ for an absolute constant $C$ and all $t$ (ideally with a polynomial-time algorithm), or a disproof: an infinite family of simple doubly $t_j$-sparse systems with $\mathrm{disc}/\sqrt{t_j} \to \infty$. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) an $n$-independent bound $L(t) = o(\sqrt{t \log t})$, i.e. $L(t) \leq \sqrt{t}\, g(t)$ with $g(t) \to \infty$ slower than $\sqrt{\log t}$, or $L(t) = O(\sqrt{t} (\log t)^{\gamma})$ for some constant $\gamma < 1/2$; (ii) a lower bound $L(t) = \omega(\sqrt{t})$ (showing that simplicity does not suffice for the Beck-Fiala bound), or a proof that the LLL bound is tight, $L(t) = \Omega(\sqrt{t \log t})$; (iii) $L(t) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for a natural infinite subclass of simple systems where it is not implied by known results, e.g. all simple doubly $t$-sparse systems with $n \leq t^{C}$ for a constant $C$ (so that $t \geq n^{1/C} \gg \log n$ is not the issue), or all simple systems with girth at least $5$ or bounded codegree structure, provided the class is not covered by the random-model results; (iv) a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $o(\sqrt{t \log t})$ for all simple doubly $t$-sparse systems, or achieving the LLL bound $O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ deterministically where only randomized/existential arguments are known; (v) removing the simplicity hypothesis: $D(t) = o(\sqrt{t \log t})$ (this is progress on Problem 1.15 for bounded set sizes). Improving constants in the LLL or Beck-Fiala bounds does not count.

literature.title: N. Alon, J. H. Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, 3rd ed., Wiley, 2008 (Chapter 5: The Local Lemma; Chapter 13: Discrepancy)
literature.description: Standard reference for the Lovász Local Lemma and for the probabilistic method in discrepancy, including the random-coloring and Beck-Fiala arguments.

literature.title: E. Ezra, S. Lovett, On the Beck-Fiala conjecture for random set systems, APPROX/RANDOM 2015; Random Structures & Algorithms 54(4):665-675, 2019
literature.description: Uses an LLL-based argument to obtain $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ for random $t$-sparse systems with $m \geq n$; the reference point that later work beats.

literature.title: A. Potukuchi, Discrepancy in random hypergraph models, arXiv:1811.01491, 2018
literature.description: Beats the LLL bound for random $t$-sparse systems: discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely for $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, R. Meka, On the discrepancy of random low degree set systems, SODA 2019; Random Structures & Algorithms 57(3):695-705, 2020
literature.description: Proves a tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ discrepancy bound for the random $t$-sparse model for the entire range of $n$ and $m$ under $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$.

literature.title: R. Hoberg, T. Rothvoss, A Fourier-analytic approach for the discrepancy of random set systems, SODA 2019; arXiv:1806.04484
literature.description: Fourier-analytic method giving $O(1)$ discrepancy for random i.i.d. set systems with $n \geq C m \log m$ elements.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

On 2026-09-20 Google Scholar search links were replaced by DOI/arXiv links, the attribution of arXiv:1810.03374 was corrected to Bansal and Meka, Potukuchi (arXiv:1811.01491) was added, and cross-references to the 2025-26 Beck-Fiala results (Problem 1.15) were added. The AimPL page states this problem informally; the formalization in mathematicalConditions is this record's.
problems.statusDetails: Post-workshop progress: for random $t$-sparse systems the LLL-type bound $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ of Ezra-Lovett was improved to $O(\sqrt{t})$ by Potukuchi (2018, $m = n$, $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$) and by Bansal-Meka (2019, all $n, m$ with $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$); Franks-Saks and Hoberg-Rothvoss treated the many-columns regime (see Problem 1.2). For worst-case sparse systems, Bansal-Jiang (2025) and Altschuler-Tikhomirov (2026) give $O(\sqrt{t})$ whenever $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$ (see Problem 1.15). A general method beating the LLL for arbitrary bounded-degree systems with $t \leq \log n$ is not known.
